name: Brachydactyly Type B

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Brachydactyly Type B

criteria.description: Congenital absence or hypoplasia of distal phalanges of fingers and toes
Hypoplasia or absence of fingernails and toenails corresponding to affected digits
Radiographic evidence showing shortened or absent distal phalanges and terminal tufts
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Identification of mutations in ROR2 gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital absence or hypoplasia of distal phalanges and corresponding nail hypoplasia confirmed by radiographic findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can confirm diagnosis but is not mandatory; family history supports diagnosis.

occasional.symptomName: Symphalangism affecting the phalanges of the hand

imaging: X-ray showing absence or hypoplasia of distal phalanges and terminal tufts
Radiographs demonstrating shortened middle and proximal phalanges
genetic: Mutations in ROR2 gene identified by molecular genetic testing
other: Clinical examination revealing absent or hypoplastic nails on affected digits

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of shortened middle phalanges rather than absent distal phalanges
Nail abnormalities less prominent or absent
Progressive resorption of distal phalanges rather than congenital absence
Often associated with systemic conditions or environmental exposures

redFlags: Progressive digital bone resorption suggesting acquired pathology
Severe functional impairment of hand or foot requiring urgent intervention
Presence of systemic abnormalities indicating syndromic association
references: Temtamy SA, McKusick VA. The Genetics of Hand Malformations. 1978.
Klopocki E, et al. Mutations in ROR2 cause brachydactyly type B. Nat Genet. 2000.
